subject: Acme Corp - Bakeoff discovery & acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today

Jordan / Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Nice conversation — wanted to capture the key takeaways and next steps so we have alignment heading into the bake-off. High level summaries below, please correct anything I missed.

Pain points / goals
- Current infra (in-house TGI + some cloud endpoints) is inconsistent: p95 latency spikes during peak loads and throughput caps create UX regressions for interactive use.
- Cost is a concern: you're trying to reduce per-token infra spend while keeping latency acceptable for product demos.
- Need predictable failover: when the primary endpoint degrades you want automated fallback to a lower-cost model without huge UX degradation.

Current stack
- Primary: in-house TGI endpoints running on mixed GPU pool (NVIDIA A100 + older cards)
- Some experiments with vLLM for low-latency workloads, but operational tooling/monitoring is immature
- Auth & data path: requests routed through Acme proxy; no user PII in prompts, but logs retained for 30 days

Success criteria (for bake-off) — please confirm these are correct:
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for 512-token generation (single-turn interactive scenarios)
- Throughput: sustain 20 concurrent interactive sessions at that latency target
- Quality: match or exceed current model responses on our 25-run eval set (we'll share prompts); acceptable rate of hallucination/regression <= 5% on critical prompts
- Cost: target <= 60% of current per-token inference cost at comparable quality/latency
- Reliability: automatic fallback to a cheaper model within 2s on p95 degradation

Benchmarks / data we'll need from Acme
- Eval prompt set (25 primary prompts + 100 longer load test prompts) — you mentioned you can share these as a JSON export
- Sample traffic profile (qps distribution, typical sequence lengths)

Our deliverables / Redwood asks
- We will produce a bake-off plan (template attached) with test harness (latency/throughput/quality) and an agent to run comparisons vs vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints.
- Please confirm target AWS region and whether you can provide short-term test keys or a staging endpoint for dataset pull during the test window.

Next steps
1) You share eval prompt set + traffic profile (Sara/Slack or Drive link) — ideally by end of day Monday 11/23
2) Redwood to send formal bake-off plan and instrumentation details by 11/24
3) Schedule a 60-min kickoff to align on acceptance criteria and test schedule (propose Tue 11/24 10:00am PT)

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx, redwood_bakeoff_requirements.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Park <sara.park@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today

Thanks Marissa — great write-up, this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency target: the product team asked for p95 <= 120ms if achievable; we understand tradeoffs and are open to 150ms if the quality/cost numbers are compelling.
- Throughput: 20 concurrent interactive sessions is accurate; for load testing we can also push higher QPS to see the knee of the curve.
- Quality: we'll share the eval set (25 prompts) + an additional 50 prompts flagged as "safety/critical" where hallucination/regression is more sensitive.

We can share the eval prompt set by EOD Monday (11/23). For staging access — we can create a short-term role/keys to a staging account in our AWS account (us-west-2) for the duration of the bake-off. I'll loop in Sara to coordinate keys and the recording of today's call.

One more ask: can you include raw p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token for each run in the bake-off CSV so our ops team can run comparative unit economics?

Jordan
Jordan Lee
Director of AI Platform — Acme Corp
jordan.lee@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today

Perfect — thanks Jordan. We'll move forward with the template and instrumentation you asked for.

Confirming our plan:
- Redwood will run three main comparison points in the bake-off:
  1) Redwood-optimized hosted endpoint (our recommended config)
  2) vLLM baseline on equivalent hardware (open implementation)
  3) Your current TGI/cloud endpoints (as you have them)

- For each run we'll report: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, end-to-end throughput (concurrent sessions), cost-per-token, and qualitative diffs for the safety/critical prompts.

Tasks / owners:
- Aditya: we'll need a small test harness and the scripts to capture p50/p95 and tokens/sec per run — can you draft the harness based on the attached template?
- Neha: can you prepare the model config recommendations and quantization profile we'll try for the hosted test (noting we want to keep functional parity with your current model family)?

Proposed schedule:
- 11/23: Acme shares eval_prompt_set.json + traffic profile + staging access details
- 11/24: Redwood sends bake-off plan + instrumentation and schedule
- 11/25–11/27: Execute runs (we can run load windows each day to avoid pulling other resources)
- 11/30: Deliver final report and recommendation

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx (same as earlier)

I'll book the 11/24 kickoff for 10:00am PT — invite coming shortly.

Best,
Marissa
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sara Park <sara.park@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today

Marissa — we uploaded the eval prompt set and traffic profile to the Drive folder and granted view access to marissa.cole@redwood.com. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-redwood-acme-bakeoff

Also attached: acme_eval_prompt_set.json (25 primary prompts) and acme_load_profile.csv. Staging keys will be delivered via Secrets Manager invite to the email you specified.

Confirming acceptance criteria update: p95 target = 120ms preferred, 150ms acceptable. For cost reporting, please include raw per-token cost and an adjusted cost assuming reserved-capacity discounts (we'll apply our internal multipliers).

Recording of today's call: https://acme.zoom.us/rec/share/abcd1234 (access for 30 days)

Thanks — Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:00:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Acme bake-off — immediate tasks

Team — quick internal note following Jordan's confirm:

1) Aditya: prioritize the test harness. Use the redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx and ensure output CSV includes p50/p95, tokens_per_sec, end_to_end_throughput, cost_per_token, and raw latency samples. Aim for a dry-run with a small subset by 11/24 EOD.

2) Neha: prepare the model config and quantization profiles. Start with fp16 and two quantized variants we can test (4-bit and 8-bit where applicable). Document any expected quality delta per prompt category.

3) I'll coordinate the kickoff invite and ensure we have a single Drive folder with the artifacts. I'll also produce the acceptance-criteria checklist that we can use during the run.

Attachments for internal: redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx, redwood_bakeoff_requirements.pdf

Marissa
